newsitem.title: DUBAI: Saudi says power consumption grows at annual 16pct.
newsitem.headline: Saudi says power consumption grows at annual 16pct.

text.p: A Saudi minister on Sunday urged the 18 million people in the kingdom to rationalise electricity use which he said was growing at an average annual 16 percent, the official Saudi Press Agency (SPA) reported on Sunday.
Minister of Industry and Electricity Hashem bin Abdullah bin Hashem Yamani said there were 122,000 new subscribers last year.
"The number of subscribers has risen to more than 3.34 million," he said.
In March the minister said electricity demand was expected to total 59,267 megawatts in 2020 from 19,573 MW in 1995.
At the time he said it would cost some $117 billion to boost generating, transmission and distribution capacity to 69,520 MW by 2020 from 19,662 MW in 1995.
Saudi Arabia is struggling to keep pace with surging electricity demand and has had on occassions in the past three years experienced black-outs in some cities during load times.
Electricity officials say air conditioning represents a large portion of consumption in the kingdom where temperatures in the summer sometimes reach 51 Celsius (124 Fahrenheit) in some areas.
